description: The line plot illustrates the relationship between a model’s BLEU score and an unspecified x-axis variable ranging from 0.0 to 10.0, likely representing a hyperparameter or training condition such as latency or consistency weight. The y-axis, labeled “BLEU,” spans from 18 to 29 with major tick marks at intervals of 2, indicating translation quality. Four methods are compared: “Consistency-CE” (purple circles, dashed line), “Inconsistency-CE” (purple squares, dashed line), “Inconsistency-CE-MP” (blue squares, dash-dot line), and “Consistency-Bi” (red stars, solid line). All methods show increasing BLEU scores as the x-axis value increases. “Consistency-Bi” starts at approximately BLEU 22.2 at x=0.0 and rises steadily to about 28.8 at x=10.0, peaking around x=8.5. “Inconsistency-CE-MP” begins at BLEU 18.5, climbs to 27.0 at x=10.0, and closely tracks “Inconsistency-CE,” which starts at BLEU 20.0 and reaches 27.0. “Consistency-CE” starts lowest at BLEU 18.8, rises to 27.2 at x=10.0, and remains below the other three methods across the range. The plot suggests that “Consistency-Bi” consistently outperforms the others, especially at higher x-values.
